title: Thankful in the Lions' Den
scripture_text: He prayed and gave thanks before his God...
devotional:
## Key Word
**Thanksgiving is not a reaction to comfort — it is a decision in the middle of the threat.**

## Word Focus
Daniel did not wait for the den to pass before he gave thanks. He prayed while the decree was signed. Gratitude was his custom, not his mood.

A thankful heart does not deny the danger — it refuses to let the danger rename God. Thank Him in the threat, and you remember who is on the throne.

This month, let thanksgiving be your daily custom. Whether the door is open or the decree is signed, kneel, pray, and give thanks. The God who kept Daniel in the den is the same God keeping you today.

## Bible Story Tie-In — Daniel
Daniel prayed three times a day with his windows open, even after the king signed the decree. His thanksgiving did not stop when the threat started.

## Prayer
Father, teach me to thank You before the answer comes.
Amen.

## Confession
- I give thanks in every season.
- My gratitude is a decision, not a mood.
- No decree can silence my praise.
- God is faithful in the den and out of it.

## Action Point
Kneel and thank God for three things before you sleep tonight.

## Quiz
- What did Daniel do when he heard about the decree?
- Why is thanksgiving a decision and not a mood?
- What will you thank God for today, before the answer comes?

— Pastor Amos

title: Thanksgiving After the Den
scripture_text: Oh, give thanks to the LORD, for He is good!
devotional:
## Key Word
**When God shuts the lions' mouths, your thanksgiving should be louder than your fear ever was.**

## Word Focus
Daniel spent the night with the lions, and morning found him unharmed. The God who kept him in the den is the God who keeps you now.

Deliverance is not the end of the story — it is the beginning of thanksgiving. When God brings you out, praise is the right response.

This month, let your thanksgiving overflow. Count the dens you have walked out of, name the lions God silenced, and thank Him out loud. A grateful heart turns every deliverance into worship.

## Bible Story Tie-In — Daniel
The king found Daniel alive at dawn and ordered the accusers thrown in instead. The God who shut the lions' mouths turned a death sentence into a decree of praise.

## Prayer
Father, thank You for shutting the lions' mouths over my life.
Amen.

## Confession
- I am delivered, and I give thanks.
- No lion can touch what God protects.
- My praise is louder than my fear.
- God turns my den into a testimony.

## Action Point
Name three deliverances from this year and thank God for each one.

## Quiz
- Who shut the lions' mouths, according to Daniel?
- What did the king decree after Daniel came out alive?
- Which deliverance will you thank God for today?

— Pastor Amos

title: The God Who Delivers
scripture_text: He delivers and rescues, and He works signs and wonders
devotional:
## Key Word
**Your deliverance was never just for you — it was so a whole kingdom could hear about your God.**

## Word Focus
Daniel did not just walk out of the den — the king wrote a decree about his God. One man's deliverance became a nation's witness.

Your testimony works the same way. When God rescues you in front of people, your praise becomes an announcement nobody can argue with.

This month, let your thanksgiving overflow in public. Tell someone what God did. The lions God silenced in your life are the proof somebody else needs to believe — and your praise is the decree that carries it to them.

## Bible Story Tie-In — Daniel
King Darius wrote to all peoples: tremble before the God of Daniel. One den, one deliverance — and the whole kingdom heard God's name.

## Prayer
Father, let my deliverance announce Your name to everyone watching.
Amen.

## Confession
- My deliverance is a witness, not a secret.
- The God of Daniel is the God who keeps me.
- My praise will carry His name further than my fear.
- Every den I leave becomes a decree of praise.

## Action Point
Tell one person today about a deliverance God gave you this year.

## Quiz
- What did King Darius decree after Daniel came out of the den?
- Why does your deliverance become a witness to others?
- Who will you tell about God's deliverance this week?

— Pastor Amos

title: Thanksgiving Before the Announcement
scripture_text: I thank You and praise You, O God of my fathers; You have given me wisdom and might
devotional:
## Key Word
**Thank God the moment you know — before the answer is announced, before the door opens, before anyone else can see it.**

## Word Focus
Daniel received the mystery in a night vision, and his first move was to thank God — before the king, before the platform.

Thanksgiving is the first response to revelation, not the last response to results. Thank Him right away — the praise locks the revelation in.

This month, let your thanksgiving run ahead of your announcements. Thank Him now, in the night, and walk into the morning already full of praise.

## Bible Story Tie-In — Daniel
Daniel thanked God in the night, then stood before the king in the morning. The praise came before the platform.

## Prayer
Father, teach me to thank You the moment You speak.
Amen.

## Confession
- I thank God the moment I know.
- My praise comes before my platform.
- What God reveals to me, I carry with thanksgiving.
- My thanksgiving opens doors my asking cannot.

## Action Point
Thank God out loud today for one thing He has shown you that no one else has seen yet.

## Quiz
- What did Daniel do first after God revealed the king's dream?
- Why does thanksgiving come before the announcement?
- What has God shown you that you have not yet thanked Him for?

— Pastor Amos

title: Blessed Be the Name of God
scripture_text: Blessed be the name of God forever and ever, for wisdom and might are His.
devotional:
## Key Word
**Bless His name in the night, before the morning comes — thanksgiving is the first sound of the delivered.**

## Word Focus
Daniel did not wait for the palace to thank God. The secret came in a night vision, and blessing rose before the sunrise.

That is the order of overflowing thanksgiving: blessing at the revelation, not after the result. Thank Him the moment you know.

This month, do not hold your praise until the door opens. Bless the name of God in the night, while the answer is still a secret, and walk into the morning already full.

## Bible Story Tie-In — Daniel
Daniel blessed God in the night for a secret no one else could see, then carried that same praise into the king's court in the morning.

## Prayer
Father, let my first response to every revelation be blessing.
Amen.

## Confession
- I bless the name of God forever.
- My thanksgiving rises in the night.
- I praise Him before the platform.
- Wisdom and might belong to my God.

## Action Point
Bless God's name out loud tonight for one secret He has shown you.

## Quiz
- What did Daniel do the moment the secret was revealed?
- Why bless God's name before the morning comes?
- What secret has God shown you that deserves blessing tonight?

— Pastor Amos

title: Thank Him for the Answer
scripture_text: You have given me wisdom and might.
devotional:
## Key Word
**Thanksgiving is the receipt of the answer — it proves you knew God heard you before you saw it.**

## Word Focus
Daniel did not wait for the palace to see the answer. He thanked God the moment the secret was revealed, and the praise rose before the result.

That is the order of overflowing thanksgiving: receive the answer with praise, not panic. What God shows in secret, thank Him for in the open.

This month, let your thanksgiving carry the weight of the answer. Before the door opens and the lions are silenced, thank Him for wisdom and might already given — the morning will confirm what the night believed.

## Bible Story Tie-In — Daniel
Daniel thanked God for wisdom and might the moment the secret was known, then stood before the king and delivered the answer boldly.

## Prayer
Father, teach me to thank You for the answer before I see it.
Amen.

## Confession
- I thank God for wisdom and might.
- My answer is received with praise.
- I will not wait for the result to rejoice.
- Thanksgiving is my first response.

## Action Point
Thank God out loud today for one answer you are still waiting to see.

## Quiz
- What did Daniel thank God for in Daniel 2:23?
- Why thank God for an answer before you see it?
- What answer are you thanking God for today?

— Pastor Amos

title: Thank Him Three Times a Day
scripture_text: Prayed and gave thanks before his God
devotional:
## Key Word
**Thanksgiving was Daniel's custom, not his reaction — he thanked God three times a day, decree or no decree.**

## Word Focus
The decree was signed and the lions were waiting, but Daniel went home, opened his windows toward Jerusalem, and knelt to pray as he always had.

Thanksgiving did not wait for the danger to pass. Daniel gave thanks in the middle of the threat, because his custom was stronger than the king's decree.

This is overflowing thanksgiving: a habit that no decree can cancel and no den can silence. When praise is your custom, the lions lose their audience — and the morning finds you still kneeling, still thanking, still standing.

## Bible Story Tie-In — Daniel
When the decree against prayer was signed, Daniel opened his windows toward Jerusalem and knelt three times that day to give thanks, as was his custom.

## Prayer
Father, make thanksgiving my custom, not my reaction.
Amen.

## Confession
- Thanksgiving is my custom.
- I pray and give thanks three times a day.
- No decree can cancel my praise.
- The lions will find me kneeling, not afraid.

## Action Point
Thank God three times today: morning, midday, and night.

## Quiz
- What was Daniel's custom in Daniel 6:10?
- Why did Daniel keep praying after the decree was signed?
- What three times today will you stop and give thanks?

— Pastor Amos

title: The Morning After the Den
scripture_text: My God sent His angel and shut the lions' mouths
devotional:
## Key Word
**The morning after the den is the sweetest thanksgiving — the lions are silent, and you are still standing.**

## Word Focus
At the break of day, Darius hurried to the den and called out with a lamenting voice: 'Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God delivered you?'

And Daniel answered from among the lions, 'O king, live forever! My God sent His angel and shut the lions' mouths.'

This is overflowing thanksgiving the morning after: you wake up alive in the place that was meant to end you, and your first words are praise. The den could not keep you, and the king himself becomes a witness to your God.

## Bible Story Tie-In — Daniel
At dawn the king hurried to the den and found Daniel alive; God had sent His angel to shut the lions' mouths, and he was lifted out unhurt.

## Prayer
Father, thank You for the morning after the den.
Amen.

## Confession
- I came out of the den unhurt.
- My God shut the lions' mouths.
- The morning found me alive and thanking.
- My deliverance will make kings believe.

## Action Point
Name one den God brought you out of and thank Him out loud today.

## Quiz
- What did Darius do at the break of day in Daniel 6:19?
- Who shut the lions' mouths, according to Daniel 6:22?
- What is your morning-after thanksgiving — the den God brought you out of?

— Pastor Amos

title: He Delivers and Rescues
scripture_text: He delivers and rescues, and He works signs and wonders
devotional:
## Key Word
**Your deliverance was not private — it became a decree, and a whole kingdom heard about your God.**

## Word Focus
When Daniel walked out of the den, the king did not keep it quiet. Darius decreed to every people and nation: tremble before the God of Daniel.

That is what overflowing thanksgiving does. A private rescue becomes a public witness, and the mouths that mocked you now confess your God.

Your testimony is not the end of your story — it is a decree in your generation. Someone waits to hear that the God who shut the lions' mouths still delivers. Tell it, and let thanksgiving overflow.

## Bible Story Tie-In — Daniel
Darius wrote to all peoples that Daniel's God delivers and rescues, and works signs and wonders in heaven and on earth.

## Prayer
Father, thank You for my deliverance — and for making it a witness.
Amen.

## Confession
- My God delivers and rescues.
- He works signs and wonders for me.
- My testimony will reach a whole kingdom.
- My thanksgiving will overflow beyond me.

## Action Point
Tell one person today the story of a deliverance God gave you.

## Quiz
- What did Darius decree in Daniel 6:26?
- According to Daniel 6:27, what does God do in heaven and on earth?
- Who needs to hear your deliverance story — and when will you tell them?

— Pastor Amos

title: Thank Him in the Night
scripture_text: The secret was revealed to Daniel in a night vision
devotional:
## Key Word
**The answer came in the night — and Daniel's first response was not relief, but blessing.**

## Word Focus
No wise man in Babylon could tell the king his dream. Daniel asked for time, went to his friends, and they sought mercy from the God of heaven.

In the night, the secret was revealed. Before Daniel told the king anything, he blessed God — thanksgiving came before the testimony.

That is overflowing thanksgiving: you thank God for the answer while it is still dark. The blessing you give in the night becomes your boldness in the morning. Thank Him now, and watch the secret become a song.

## Bible Story Tie-In — Daniel
Daniel 2:19 says the secret was revealed to Daniel in a night vision, and he blessed the God of heaven before he ever stood before the king.

## Prayer
Father, thank You for answers that come in the night.
Amen.

## Confession
- God reveals secrets in the night.
- My first response is blessing, not fear.
- I thank Him before the morning comes.
- The answer I receive will become my song.

## Action Point
Thank God tonight for one answer you are still waiting for.

## Quiz
- What did Daniel and his friends do in Daniel 2:17-18?
- According to Daniel 2:19, when was the secret revealed?
- What answer are you thanking God for before you see it?

— Pastor Amos

title: Bless His Name Forever
scripture_text: Blessed be the name of God forever and ever
devotional:
## Key Word
**Daniel blessed God before the king ever heard the answer. Thanksgiving is the first testimony.**

## Word Focus
The secret was revealed in the night, and Daniel did not run to the palace. He stopped to bless the God who gave the answer.

His prayer named what God is: wisdom and might belong to Him. He changes the times and the seasons; He gives wisdom to the wise.

That is overflowing thanksgiving: you bless His name before the outcome is visible to anyone else. Your praise in private becomes your confidence in public. Bless His name now — forever is already settled.

## Bible Story Tie-In — Daniel
Daniel 2:20-23 records Daniel blessing God after the night vision — wisdom and might are His, and He reveals deep and secret things.

## Prayer
Father, thank You for wisdom and might that belong to You alone.
Amen.

## Confession
- I bless the name of God forever.
- Wisdom and might belong to Him.
- My thanksgiving comes before my testimony.
- What He reveals in the night, I will declare in the morning.

## Action Point
Write down three answers God gave you this year and bless His name for each one.

## Quiz
- According to Daniel 2:20, what two things belong to God?
- What did Daniel do first after the secret was revealed? (Daniel 2:20-23)
- What three answers from this year are you blessing God for today?

— Pastor Amos

title: There Is a God in Heaven
scripture_text: But there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets
devotional:
## Key Word
**The God who reveals secrets will make even kings confess His name — thank Him before the world sees it.**

## Word Focus
Daniel took no credit for the secret. He pointed the king to heaven: the answer was God's, not his, and the glory belonged to God alone.

Thanksgiving that gives God the glory turns a private answer into a public witness. What He did for you in secret, He will use to speak to others.

When you thank God openly for what only He could do, unbelievers hear His name. Your testimony becomes the king's confession, and a palace becomes a pulpit. That is overflowing thanksgiving.

## Bible Story Tie-In — Daniel
Daniel told the king the secret was revealed by the God in heaven — and the king answered, "Truly your God is the God of gods" (Daniel 2:28, 47).

## Prayer
Father, thank You for revealing what no man could know.
Amen.

## Confession
- There is a God in heaven who reveals secrets.
- What no man could know, He has made known to me.
- I will not take the credit — the glory is His.
- Kings will hear His name through my thanksgiving.

## Action Point
Tell one person today about an answer only God could give.

## Quiz
- According to Daniel 2:28, who reveals secrets?
- What did King Nebuchadnezzar confess in Daniel 2:47?
- Name one answer only God could give that you will share today.

— Pastor Amos

title: Take Off Your Shoes
scripture_text: The place where you stand is holy ground
devotional:
## Key Word
**The burning bush was not a show — it was a summons: take off your shoes, for ordinary ground becomes holy when God speaks.**

## Word Focus
Moses turned aside to see a bush that burned without burning out — and God called his name. The fire was not the message; the voice in the fire was.

God told him to remove his shoes — the ground was holy. Reverence is not fear of God; it is the honour you give the One who is speaking.

The encounter did not end in wonder — it ended in a commission. God was sending Moses back to Egypt. Hear this: every true encounter carries an assignment. Take off your shoes, hear His voice, and go.

## Bible Story Tie-In — Moses
Moses hid his face, afraid to look upon God — yet the God who said 'I AM' sent him back to Pharaoh with a staff, a word, and a promise.

## Prayer
Father, teach me to honour Your presence and obey Your voice.
Amen.

## Confession
- I honour the holiness of God.
- I take off my shoes — I will not treat holy ground as common.
- I listen to His voice, and I obey what He says.
- Every encounter with God sends me with a purpose.

## Action Point
Obey one instruction from God today that you have been delaying.

## Quiz
- What did Moses see burning in the wilderness?
- Why did God tell Moses to remove his shoes?
- What assignment followed Moses' encounter with God?

— Pastor Amos

title: When the King Reveals Himself
scripture_text: Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts
devotional:
## Key Word
**You cannot see the King and stay the same — the vision that shows you His glory also shows you yourself, and then it sends you.**

## Word Focus
Isaiah saw the Lord high and lifted up, and the vision exposed him: 'Woe is me, for I am undone.' Revelation shows you the King, then it shows you.

Then the coal from the altar touched his lips, and his iniquity was taken away. God does not expose you to shame you — He cleanses you to send you.

Then the Lord asked, 'Whom shall I send?' and Isaiah answered, 'Here am I; send me.' Hear this: the throne room is not the end of the journey — it is where worship becomes mission. See the King, be cleansed, and go.

## Bible Story Tie-In — Isaiah
The seraphim touched Isaiah's lips with a live coal from the altar — his sin was purged, and the cleansed man became the sent man.

## Prayer
Lord, show me Your glory, cleanse my lips, and send me.
Amen.

## Confession
- I have seen the King, and I will never be the same.
- His fire has cleansed my lips and my life.
- I am available for His purpose.
- Here am I, Lord — send me.

## Action Point
Write down one area of kingdom service you will give yourself to.

## Quiz
- What did Isaiah see in the year King Uzziah died?
- What did the live coal from the altar do?
- What did Isaiah answer when the Lord asked, 'Whom shall I send?'

— Pastor Amos

title: The Cost of Extravagant Worship
scripture_text: She has done what she could
devotional:
## Key Word
**She broke the box because she knew His worth — true worship is not measured by what it costs you, but by what He is worth to you.**

## Word Focus
She carried an alabaster box worth a year's wages, broke it, and poured it on Jesus. The room called it waste. Heaven called it worship.

Men counted the cost; Jesus counted the heart. She gave what was precious, personal, and costly — not to impress people, but to honour the King.

Our altar is surrender. Our response is obedience. Our lives are His. Extravagant worship is not a performance — it is a life poured out, and Jesus remembers it wherever the gospel is preached.

## Bible Story Tie-In — The Alabaster Box
Jesus defended her: 'She has done what she could.' What the world calls waste, the King calls a good work — and her devotion became a memorial.

## Prayer
Lord Jesus, You are worthy of my best — I give it willingly.
Amen.

## Confession
- Jesus Christ is worthy of my devotion.
- I give God my best, not my leftovers.
- My worship is not a performance for people.
- What I pour out for Him will never be wasted.

## Action Point
Offer God something costly today: your time, your attention, your best.

## Quiz
- What did the woman pour on Jesus?
- Why did some in the room call her act a waste?
- What did Jesus say her devotion would become?

— Pastor Amos

title: The Sound of Many Waters
scripture_text: Alleluia! For the Lord God Omnipotent reigns!
devotional:
## Key Word
**The sound of heaven is not noise — it is a multitude declaring one truth: the Lord God Almighty reigns.**

## Word Focus
John heard a sound like many waters and mighty thunder — a multitude declaring that the Lord God Almighty reigns. Heaven's sound is truth.

Our sound must carry the same weight. A song may be beautiful, but if it does not declare His greatness, it is only music. True worship declares the King.

This is what God is saying to Tribe X: our voices, our instruments, our arrangements must serve one purpose — declaring His greatness. When our sound carries truth, heaven joins in. Our sound is His praise.

## Bible Story Tie-In — John
A voice came out of the throne, saying, 'Praise our God, all you His servants' — and the multitude answered with a sound like many waters.

## Prayer
Father, let my voice declare Your greatness and nothing else.
Amen.

## Confession
- The Lord God Almighty reigns.
- My voice honours the King.
- My worship declares His greatness.
- I join the multitude in praising Him.

## Action Point
Read Revelation 19:1–7 and praise God for who He is.

## Quiz
- What is the sound of the multitude compared to?
- What is the central declaration of Revelation 19:6?
- Why must our worship stay centred on God's greatness?

— Pastor Amos

title: Worship That Shifts the Atmosphere
scripture_text: Praise the LORD, For His mercy endures forever
devotional:
## Key Word
**Worship is faith with a sound — sing before the battle is won.**

## Word Focus
Jehoshaphat faced an army he could not defeat, so he sought the Lord — and God said the battle was His. Then the king sent singers ahead of the soldiers.

They sang as they marched, and as they began to sing, the Lord set ambushes against the enemy. Faith does not wait for victory to sing — it sings on the way.

This is what God is saying: your worship is not a reaction to the outcome — it is your confidence in the One who has already decided it. When you sing before the change, the atmosphere shifts before the battle ends.

## Bible Story Tie-In — Jehoshaphat
Jehoshaphat sent singers before the army, praising the beauty of holiness — and as they sang, the Lord set ambushes and the enemy fell.

## Prayer
Father, strengthen my faith — I will worship before the victory.
Amen.

## Confession
- God is my confidence.
- I will not be ruled by fear.
- I trust God's Word before I see the outcome.
- My worship shifts the atmosphere around me.

## Action Point
Find one promise for your hardest situation and praise God for it.

## Quiz
- What did Jehoshaphat do when the enemy came against Judah?
- Who went before the army, and what did they sing?
- What happened as the people began to sing and praise?

— Pastor Amos

title: When Praise Becomes a Weapon
scripture_text: At midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God
devotional:
## Key Word
**Praise is a weapon — it breaks chains before the doors open.**

## Word Focus
Beaten and chained in the inner prison, Paul and Silas prayed and sang at midnight — not because they were free, but while still bound.

Principalities cannot cage a man of principle. The prison held their bodies, but it could not hold their devotion — and their praise shook the foundations.

Then the doors opened, the chains fell — and the jailer and his household found salvation. This is what God is saying: your midnight praise is not only your deliverance, it is somebody else's doorway to Jesus.

## Bible Story Tie-In — Paul and Silas
At midnight they sang, the earth shook, the doors opened, and every chain was loosed — and the jailer asked, 'What must I do to be saved?'

## Prayer
Father, let my praise rise at midnight and set others free.
Amen.

## Confession
- My worship is not controlled by circumstances.
- I remain faithful under pressure.
- No chain can hold a worshipper.
- My praise opens doors for others to find Jesus.

## Action Point
Worship today for someone in a hard season, and encourage them.

## Quiz
- Where were Paul and Silas when they worshipped?
- What happened after their prayer and praise?
- How did their praise open a door for the jailer?

— Pastor Amos

title: The Ministry of the Holy Spirit
scripture_text: He will guide you into all truth
devotional:
## Key Word
**The Holy Spirit is not a mood or a moment — He is the Person who shows you things to come and glorifies Jesus.**

## Word Focus
Jesus promised the Spirit of truth, who guides us into all truth and shows us things to come. The Spirit does not draw attention to Himself — He reveals Jesus.

Atmosphere can move emotions, but only the Holy Spirit opens vision. He shows you what God is saying and what is coming — that is the ministry of the Spirit.

So we gather our vision materials from the Spirit, not from the atmosphere: rehearsed in skill, surrendered in spirit, governed by the Word. When the Spirit leads, Christ is glorified — and that is the only measure of true worship.

## Bible Story Tie-In — The Holy Spirit
Jesus said the Spirit 'will guide you into all truth... and He will tell you things to come.' The Spirit's work is always to glorify Jesus.

## Prayer
Holy Spirit, guide me into truth and glorify Jesus through my life.
Amen.

## Confession
- The Holy Spirit guides me into all truth.
- Jesus Christ is glorified through my life.
- I remain grounded in Scripture.
- I serve with humility and sensitivity to the Spirit.

## Action Point
Read John 16:7–15 and write down what the Spirit does.

## Quiz
- What does Jesus call the Holy Spirit in John 16:13?
- Whom does the Holy Spirit glorify?
- Why must worship stay grounded in Scripture?

— Pastor Amos

title: Worship in Spirit and Truth
scripture_text: Those who worship Him must worship in spirit and truth
devotional:
## Key Word
**God is not looking for a performance — He is seeking worshippers whose life agrees with their song.**

## Word Focus
True worshippers worship in spirit and in truth. Spirit without truth is noise; truth without spirit is cold. God seeks a heart on fire, governed by His Word.

The song must agree with the life. You cannot sing forgiveness while holding hatred, or sing surrender while refusing to obey.

This is what God is saying: integrity is the sound He seeks. Worship that changes nothing is only sound. Let your private life agree with your public confession, and your worship will carry weight in heaven and on earth.

## Bible Story Tie-In — The Samaritan Woman
The Father seeks true worshippers — and Jesus said the hour is now. The life behind the song must agree with the message of the song.

## Prayer
Father, let my worship be sincere — my life agreeing with my song.
Amen.

## Confession
- I worship God in spirit and in truth.
- My private life agrees with my public confession.
- God's Word governs my conduct.
- My worship is sincere.

## Action Point
Take one song you sing and check your life against its message.

## Quiz
- What two dimensions of worship did Jesus name?
- Why must spirit be governed by truth?
- How does integrity strengthen our worship?

— Pastor Amos

title: The Priesthood of Every Believer
scripture_text: Has made us kings and priests to His God and Father
devotional:
## Key Word
**How dare you be ordinary? You are a king and a priest.**

## Word Focus
Jesus loved us, washed us in His blood, and made us kings and priests to God. Access to the throne is not bought by talent — it was purchased by blood.

Tonight Tribe X gathers before the throne — not as spectators, but as priests. You do not need a microphone to worship; you need a life surrendered to Christ.

So come boldly. Bring your voice, bring your life, bring your surrender — the King is on the throne, and His priests are gathering. Road to the Throne Room: tonight, we stand before Him together.

## Bible Story Tie-In — John
John declared Christ 'has made us kings and priests to His God and Father' — by His blood, not our works. Tonight, every believer comes as a priest.

## Prayer
Lord Jesus, thank You for making me a priest — I come boldly.
Amen.

## Confession
- Jesus Christ has redeemed me.
- I am a king and a priest unto God.
- My identity is established in Him.
- My life is devoted to His glory.

## Action Point
Come to Tribe X tonight as a priest — bring your surrender.

## Quiz
- What has Jesus made us, according to Revelation 1:6?
- What purchased our access to God?
- Why does every believer need personal devotion?

— Pastor Amos
